title: Customer-tiered geo routing override and delegation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Enterprise customers require deterministic control over where their inference traffic is served (region+tier) while still allowing Redwood to apply automated fallbacks when capacity or latency targets cannot be met. Current geo routing enforces account-level residency but lacks a scoped, auditable mechanism for per-customer overrides, delegated endpoints (customer-managed VPC/default passthrough), and an ordered policy evaluator that preserves compliance guarantees (e.g., EU-only) while enabling emergency escape modes.
background: We have several related tickets addressing territory routing, tenant allowlists, and emergency fallback strategies, but customers keep asking for: 1) per-customer policy overrides with explicit audit logs, 2) ability to delegate to a customer-managed endpoint for certain request classes, and 3) predictable precedence rules so that overrides cannot silently bypass data residency constraints. This ticket designs and implements a new scoped override/override-delegation flow with precedence rules, RBAC checks, and an audit chain.
goals: Introduce per-customer routing override records that are evaluated at request-time
Add a delegation mechanism where requests can be routed to customer-managed endpoints when authorized
Define and implement a clear policy precedence graph that prevents overrides from violating residency constraints unless an emergency escape is explicitly approved
Emit structured audit events for every evaluated override and delegation decision
Ship with integration tests, canary rollout, and feature flag gating
non_goals: Allow ad-hoc bypasses of legal/regulatory residency requirements
Replace global tenant residency enforcement (this augments it with scoped overrides and guardrails)
policy_precedence: 1. Explicit account-level non-overrideable residency (hard residency mandate)
2. Explicit customer override record (scoped to model/tier/route) — allowed only if residency constraint satisfied or tagged as emergency-approved
5. Emergency delegation/passthrough when an approved emergency token is present
implementation_notes: Data model: new DB table `customer_routing_overrides` (id, customer_id, scope, target_region, target_tier, delegate_endpoint, created_by, approved_by, approval_token, expires_at, audit_fields)
Policy eval: implement PolicyEvaluator v2 that returns (route_decision, override_id, audit_reason). Default fast-path for requests that have no overrides
Delegation: delegate_endpoint must be a validated, KMS-encrypted URL entry in customer config. Runtime will establish mTLS when delegating to customer-managed endpoints
Audit: every evaluation emits a structured audit event to kafka topic `routing-audit.v2` with correlation id and decision path
RBAC: only users with `account.admin` + `routing:override` can create overrides. Approvals require `security.approver` for emergency modes
Feature flag: `geo_customer_override` to gate rollout; start internal canary for 2 weeks before enabling for early access customers
tradeoffs: Allowing per-customer overrides increases policy surface area and risk of misconfiguration (possible compliance violations). We mitigate with: approval flows, non-overridable residency flags, short expiry defaults, and strong audit trails. Delegation to customer endpoints reduces Redwood's control over execution environment — we mandate mTLS and connectivity checks, and restrict delegation to only allowed routes (no system-admin routes).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): schema + PolicyEvaluator v2 behind flag; unit/integration tests; internal canary (corp infra only)
Phase 2 (week 3-4): enable for 3 pilot customers under NDA; gather metrics (route rejection, latency delta, audit volume)
Phase 3 (week 5-6): expand to Early Access; enable delegation for pilot only; security review complete
Phase 4 (week 7+): general availability; default expiry turned on; observability dashboards public
metrics_and_alerting: latency p50/p95 delta when delegation is used
audit-event volume and missing audit errors
policy-eval fallback rate (how often system fallback triggered due to override mismatch)
acceptance_criteria: PolicyEvaluator v2 deployed behind flag and returns deterministic decision with override_id when present
Audit events emitted for each request with override evaluation (stored for 90 days in observability)
Delegation flow performs mTLS handshake and validates customer endpoint (integration test coverage)
RBAC + approval UI hooks present (PM/Design follow-up ticket created)
E2E tests confirming residency-hard-mandate cannot be bypassed by override
Rollout can be toggled per-cluster via feature flag and owner group
testing_plan: Unit tests for DB migrations and validation logic
Integration tests for PolicyEvaluator v2 (simulate override records + emergency tokens + delegation endpoints)
Chaos test: simulate region depletion to ensure fallback respects ordered precedence
Security test: attempt to create overrides without approval and assert deny
Perf test: measure policy eval latency added (goal < 2ms median)
